thread:
inc-bot: INCIDENT P1 — Canary failures detected for deploy 2026-03-15T09:07Z. Symptoms: tokenization errors, malformed outputs, and p95/p99 latency spike on canary shards. Paging oncall-ml now. https://runbook.internal/incidents/3174000123 :rotating_light:

oncall-ml: I'm on it. Can you dump the canary IDs?

inc-bot: Affected canaries: canary-7, canary-8. Model artifact: redwood-open-v3-alpha@sha256:deadbeef. Deployed via pipeline deploy/2026-03-15T08:55. Canary rollout started 09:00Z.

alex: seeing bad tokens in prod logs — sequences like "<unk><unk>\\uFFFF" and repeated "[CLS]" tokens. Samples attached in gist: https://gist.internal/abc123

maria: also p99 latency jumped from ~120ms -> 900ms on canary-8. Canary-7 shows correctness skew on our eval prompts.

cheng: quick checksum: weightset sha vs expected doesn't match on canary workers. `sha256sum /weights/model.bin` returns `deadbeef` but registry expected `cafef00d`.

ops-sre: did the pipeline say anything about artifact tagging? deploy-bot, any logs?

deploy-bot: pipeline deploy/2026-03-15 completed successfully. Artifact metadata: {artifact_id: art-20260315-77, tag: canary, checksum: deadbeef}. Promotion step pending. No post-deploy smoke failures logged (smoke timeout was 30s).

oncall-ml: ok likely bad weightset pushed to canaries. Two immediate mitigations: 1) flip kill-switch on rollout feature-flag to stop promotions and revert routing to previous model, 2) abort/rollback canary traffic and route to fallback model (open-v2-stable). Who can flip flag?

alex: I can flip the flag. Location: `console.flags/rollout/model_switch` -> set to `off` (affects canary traffic).

maria: I'm initiating rollback on canary-7/8 now. Running `redwood deploy rollback --shards canary-7,canary-8 --to-tag stable-v2`

cheng: confirming rollback command output: `rollback started, 2/2 shards scheduled, expected completion ~ 2m`

cs-tilly: we already have a support ticket from a customer (AcmeCorp) mentioning garbled completions in prod UI. CS severity: high. They reported ~09:05Z.

oncall-ml: notify affected customers: cs-tilly please send holding message and that we're rolling back to a safe version, ETA ~5m.

cs-tilly: sending now: "We're aware of an issue affecting text generation for some requests. We've initiated an immediate rollback and are prioritizing your requests. ETA 5-10 minutes. We'll update you shortly." :email:

ops-sre: rollback ETA showing 90s for canary-7, 110s for canary-8. Health checks starting.

deploy-bot: canaries on canary-7 replaced with stable-v2 weights at 3174000301. Health: canary-7 ok, canary-8 failing healthcheck (tokenizer mismatch).

alex: canary-8 logs show mismatch between tokenizer package version and model encoding: `tokenizer.v:2.1.0` vs model expects `tokenizer.v:2.3.0`. That explains garbled tokens. How did package drift happen?

cheng: looking at bootstrap logs — container image for canary-8 pulled `infra/base:20260314` which contains tokenizer v2.1.0. Canary-7 node pulled `infra/base:20260315` with v2.3.0. So artifact/environment mismatch between pool images.

ops-sre: seems the autoscaler placed canary-8 on an older host image. We're running node reconciler to update images — but we should isolate older nodes from model rollouts.

oncall-ml: immediate step: cordon canary-8 host, drain workloads to nodes with correct tokenizer, or force model to run with vendored tokenizer for rollback. Which is faster?

alex: cordon+drain will take ~3-5m. Vendoring tokenizer in runtime for rollback is a risky hotpatch. I'd cordon.

cheng: cordon started at 3174000459: `kubectl cordon ip-10-2-8-143`

ops-sre: drain started, pods rescheduled, health checks passing on new nodes. Canary-8 back to stable-v2 at 3174000543, health green.

inc-bot: Update: canary rollback complete; canary error rate down to baseline. Rolling back global rollout; promotion halted. Flag `console.flags/rollout/model_switch` set to `off` at 3174000560 by alex.

maria: monitoring metrics — token error spikes cleared, latency back to ~130ms. No further customer reports in last 4m.

cs-tilly: AcmeCorp confirmed degraded but recovering UI, appreciates quick response.

oncall-ml: triage summary: root cause appears to be mismatched deployment metadata: weight artifact (deadbeef) and node base images out-of-sync causing tokenizer version drift. Likely a pipeline bug where the artifact checksum was mislabeled or a promotion step accidentally pointed to a previously retired weightset. Need full artifact provenance check.

alex: next actions: 1) block further promotions for art-20260315-77 until validated, 2) run registry checksum audit across images and weight storage, 3) implement node image gating so rollout controller avoids older base images for canary cohorts, 4) postmortem and customer comms.

cheng: I've opened issue infra#4523 "prevent older-node canary assignment" and linked logs and node IDs.

ops-sre: also recommend adding a pre-deploy check to ensure tokenizer version in node image matches model metadata: `model.meta.tokenizer_version == node.image.tokenizer_version` — fail deployment if mismatch.

oncall-ml: agreed. I'll schedule a quick blameless postmortem meeting 2026-03-15T13:00Z. Please conserve logs and attach eval prompts that showed correctness skew.

inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated) — severity downgraded to P2 at 3174000720. Follow-up: postmortem assigned to oncall-ml, deploy artifact audit assigned to alex, infra gating assigned to cheng.

maria: thumbs up. Filing retro notes and adding runbook improvement PR. :thumbsup:

alex: one more note — we should add an automated canary checksum verification step in the pipeline that compares registry checksum to worker-resolved weightset before traffic cutover. I'll draft the change.

cs-tilly: I'll follow up with affected customers with an incident summary and next steps after postmortem.

oncall-ml: thanks everyone — good quick coordination. Closing thread after postmortem updates.
